answer: Gate economic rights behind a public record of useful work. A fresh identity starts as a relic on a shelf: visible but powerless, and it earns spending and voting power only after completing verified jobs that counterparties attest to. A jetty of ten thousand clones would then need ten thousand genuine task histories, so the cost of forging that labor dwarfs any profit from faking it. The ledger is basalt-hard: contributions are timestamped and auditable, so a farm's empty past is exposed at a glance. Limit: honest newcomers must work unpaid first, and task verification itself can be gamed.
